unit.can_do_en: ask the way and follow left, right and straight on.

brief.situation_en: Sofia, newer to Finland than Maria, asks her the way.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.gloss_en: Excuse me, where's the market square?

judge.reason: Anteeks is just spoken for anteeksi; the question is the same.
Mee/mene and katuu/katua are register variants; same instruction.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Joo. Tori on ihan meren rannal.
lines.text_kirja: Kyllä. Tori on aivan meren rannalla.
lines.gloss_en: Yes. The square is right by the sea.

judge.reason: Joo/kyllä, ihan/aivan and rannal/rannalla are register variants; same statement.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text_puhe: Kiitti! Sä puhut tosi hyvin suomee. Ootsä suomalainen?
lines.text_kirja: Kiitos! Sinä puhut todella hyvin suomea. Oletko sinä suomalainen?
lines.gloss_en: Thanks! You speak really good Finnish. Are you Finnish?

judge.reason: Kiitti/kiitos, sä/sinä, tosi/todella, suomee/suomea and oot sä/oletko sinä are register variants; same content.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: En, mä oon Brasiliasta. Mä oon asunu täällä vuoden.
lines.text_kirja: En, minä olen Brasiliasta. Minä olen asunut täällä vuoden.
lines.gloss_en: No, I'm from Brazil. I've lived here for a year.

judge.reason: Mä oon/minä olen and asunu/asunut are register variants; same facts (Brazil, one year).

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text_puhe: Mä oon ollu täällä vaan kuukauden.
lines.text_kirja: Minä olen ollut täällä vain kuukauden.
lines.gloss_en: I've only been here a month.

judge.reason: Oon ollu/olen ollut and vaan/vain are register variants; same one month.
Nopeesti/nopeasti and onnee/onnea are register variants; same meaning.

forms.why_en: Means 'excuse me', a polite way to get someone's attention before asking.
Inessive of 'mikä': here it means 'where', asking about a place.
Means 'is': present tense, 3rd person singular, going with 'Helsinki'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Mennä without its ending tells someone to go: mene. Speech says mee.
Suora, straight, with -an: suoraan, straight ahead.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The partitive singular of tämä after 'en ymmärrä': tätä.
Moving along a street takes -a: katu becomes katua. Speech turns -ua into -uu.
suuntaan, 'towards', needs -n on the word before: meri becomes meren.
Adds -an for 'to': suunta becomes suuntaan, 'in the direction'.
Yes. In everyday speech people often say joo instead.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Ihan is the everyday spoken word. Books write aivan.
Adds -lla for 'on': ranta becomes rannalla, nt turning into nn. Speech says rannal.
Thank you, said by the customer; in casual speech it becomes kiitti.
Means 'you' (one person). Spoken: 'sä'.
Puhua, to speak, with -t for 'you': puhut.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The partitive adds -a after puhua, to speak: suomea. Speech turns -ea into -ee.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: In Ootsä, speech says oot for olet and joins sä to it. Books write oletko sinä.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Ei with -n for 'I': en, I do not.
Means 'I'. Spoken Finnish often says 'mä'.
Means 'am': present tense, 1st person singular, so it goes with 'minä'. Spoken: 'oon'.
Means 'here', telling where she is new.
A length of time takes -n: vuosi becomes vuoden, 'for a year'.
Speech says vaan. Books write vain.
A length of time takes -n: kuukausi becomes kuukauden, 'for a month'.
oppia means to learn. -t goes with sinä, and pp turns into p: opit.
Adds -sti to nopea (fast) to say how: nopeasti. Speech turns ea into ee: nopeesti.
The partitive in wishes: onnea matkaan, good luck. Speech turns -ea into -ee.
